title: AlphaQubit: neural decoder beats matching decoders on Sycamore data
who: Google DeepMind + Google Quantum AI · Nature
what: Transformer decoder for the surface code. On real experimental data at distance 3 and 5 it made 6% fewer errors than tensor-network decoders and 30% fewer than correlated matching; simulated up to distance 11.
artifact: Decoding of real quantum-processor data (offline, not real-time)
caveat: Not real-time in this version; decoding is one component of error correction. The 6% is the paper's distance-5 result (2.748% vs 2.915% logical error per round against the tensor-network decoder); the 30% against correlated matching is Google's blog figure, which the paper's text does not state (correlated-matching rates appear only in Fig. 3).

title: AlphaQubit 2: real-time neural decoding under 1 µs per cycle on TPUs
who: Google DeepMind + Google Quantum AI · arXiv 2512.07737
what: Near-optimal logical error rates on simulated surface codes to distance 23; colour codes decoded to distance 27, where the paper says the result 'does not match the idealized trend'. A compact variant decodes in under 1 µs per cycle (throughput; latency below 500 µs) up to distance 11 on Trillium TPUs. On recorded Willow data (d = 3, 5, 7) it matches AlphaQubit 1 and beats Libra.
artifact: Offline decoding of Willow data; real-time variant demonstrated on TPUs
caveat: Applied to recorded chip data, not yet in a live Willow experiment. 'Under 1 µs per cycle' is throughput (average time per cycle), not latency, which the paper puts below 500 µs.

title: AlphaEvolve quantum circuits with 10× lower error, run on Willow for molecular simulation
who: Google DeepMind · AlphaEvolve impact report, May 7 2026; experiment: Google Quantum AI et al., arXiv 2510.19550 (v1 22 Oct 2025)
what: The Gemini-driven evolutionary coder evolved a Trotter-circuit generator whose circuits cut the mean approximation error against exact classical simulation from 10.4% to 0.82% within the device's gate budget (the report's '10x lower error'). DeepMind says the circuits enabled molecular simulations on the Willow processor that supported first-of-a-kind experimental demonstrations.
artifact: Circuits executed on Google's Willow quantum processor
caveat: Google's own report; the underlying experiment paper is not named in the post. The post links arXiv 2510.19550 (first submitted 22 Oct 2025), where the figure is simulation-approximation error under a gate budget, scored against a classically pre-computed dataset of OTOCs; the preprint is the company's own, with 323 authors.

title: qBraid × AlphaEvolve: fermion-to-qubit encodings reach distance 5 where hand design reached 3
who: qBraid · arXiv 2606.25870
what: AlphaEvolve edited a seed program that builds encodings from a molecule's interaction graph. Reported: 4.2–5× fewer data qubits for the same protection and 3.4–7.9× lower logical error under exact decoding; held-out BeH₂ and H₂O kept distance 5.
artifact: None; evaluated by exhaustive enumeration and exact decoding
caveat: Simulation only; circuit-level fault tolerance listed as next step

title: Language model generates blueprints for quantum-optics experiments, two of them new
who: University of Tübingen (Arlt, Krenn group) · Nature Machine Intelligence (published 19 Feb 2026)
what: A transformer trained on state-to-blueprint pairs writes Python that constructs an experiment for a whole class of target states. Valid rules for 6 of 20 classes (GHZ, W, Bell among them); 4 matched known solutions, 2 were new.
artifact: None; designs checked by simulated fidelity
caveat: Not built in a lab. The model is a 133-million-parameter transformer trained from random initialization on synthetic state–blueprint pairs, not a general-purpose language model; journal publication 19 February 2026 (arXiv June 2024).

title: GPT-5 supplies the key idea for a quantum-complexity bound (QMA amplification)
who: Aaronson, Witteveen · arXiv 2509.21131
what: Black-box QMA amplification cannot beat doubly-exponential completeness error; the model proposed the construction, humans proved it.
caveat: Pure complexity theory

title: Astra: exponential parallel repetition for entangled games, Lean-certified
who: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra · openai/ten-proofs
what: One of ten Lean-certified results released Aug 1 2026; extends the parallel-repetition guarantee to players sharing entanglement.
caveat: Quantum information theory, no hardware

title: Claude finds a key-recovery attack on HAWK; the scheme is withdrawn from NIST's post-quantum process
who: Anthropic (Weis), confirmed by Apon · NIST pqc-forum, July 28 2026
what: Reduces HAWK-n to SVP in dimension n/2+1; HAWK-512 security from 2^150 to 2^108; a HAWK-256 key recovered in hours. HAWK team withdrew the next day.
artifact: None physical; a real-world standards consequence
caveat: Not physics; included because it is the clearest case of an LLM changing something outside a paper

title: GNoME predicts 2.2 million crystals; 736 match later experimental entries; A-Lab synthesizes 36 of 57 targets (corrected from 41 of 58)
who: Google DeepMind, LBNL A-Lab · Nature
what: Graph-network screening found 381,000 predicted-stable structures; the 736 'independently realized' structures are matches between GNoME predictions and entries that reached the ICSD after the March 2021 snapshot, not prospective tests. Berkeley's autonomous lab made 36 of 57 chosen targets in 17 days (41 of 58 as first published; corrected 19 January 2026).
caveat: Cheetham & Seshadri (Chem. Mater. 2024) found few new or useful materials among the predictions, mostly compositional variants; Palgrave questioned several A-Lab syntheses. Nature author correction of 19 Jan 2026 (Nature 650, E1, to the A-Lab paper 10.1038/s41586-023-06734-w): 'novel' meant new to the prediction platform, not necessarily new to science; a post-publication re-analysis confirmed 36 of the 40 reported successes, four being inconclusive by XRD, and one compound (Zn2Cr3FeO8) was removed as mistakenly included in the training data. GNoME paper: 10.1038/s41586-023-06735-9.

title: Microsoft + PNNL screen 32 million candidates to 18 and synthesize a sodium-lithium solid electrolyte
who: Microsoft Azure Quantum Elements, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory · J. Am. Chem. Soc. 146, 20009 (2024)
what: AI screening plus HPC filtering produced a candidate electrolyte that was synthesized and tested in a prototype cell within months.
caveat: Company-reported; a candidate, not a product. Peer-reviewed later: Chen et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 146(29), 20009–20018, published 9 July 2024 (10.1021/jacs.4c03849); the January 2024 announcement predates the paper.

title: MatterGen designs TaCr₂O₆; synthesized with bulk modulus within 20% of target
who: Microsoft Research, SIAT Shenzhen · Nature
what: A diffusion model generated a structure for a target bulk modulus of 200 GPa; the synthesized (disordered) compound's bulk modulus was estimated at up to 169 GPa, the maximum of four nanoindentation measurements (158 ± 11 GPa) of Young's modulus converted with a DFT-computed Poisson ratio of 0.30.
caveat: One demonstration compound. The 169 GPa is inferred, not measured directly: Young's modulus by nanoindentation, a DFT Poisson ratio, and the maximum of four readings taken because the powder sample is 'likely non-compact'. Juelsholt (Materials Horizons 13, 5672, 2026; ChemRxiv preprint June 2025) argues the disordered product is the known Ta1/2Cr1/2O2 phase, reported in 1971 (1972 in the preprint's abstract) and present in MatterGen's training data.

title: AlphaEvolve: a circuit design fabricated into a TPU; ~4× faster ML force fields at Schrödinger; multi-fold lithography speedups at Substrate
who: Google DeepMind · AlphaEvolve impact report, May 7 2026
what: The Gemini-driven system is a standing tool in next-generation TPU design and one of its circuits is in silicon. Partners report ~4× speedups in training and inference of machine-learned force fields and multi-fold runtime gains in computational lithography.
artifact: Silicon; faster simulation pipelines for chemistry and chip manufacturing
caveat: Partner-reported figures; no new material or compound named

title: Lila Sciences' AI-run lab synthesizes 2,942 catalysts and finds palladium families for green-hydrogen electrolysis
who: Lila Sciences · arXiv 2609.30133, Sept 24 2026
what: An in-house proposer combining Bayesian methods with language models chose each cycle's compositions; automated PVD synthesis, screening and characterization. Six palladium-oxide families near the activity–stability frontier; InMnPdOₓ stayed below 0.5 V overpotential for over 1,000 hours in 1 M sulfuric acid.
caveat: Company preprint; 'comparable to ruthenium' is their comparison, no benchmark numbers given; humans still moved samples. The preprint (arXiv 2609.30133) does give benchmark numbers, all against films made on the same platform: InMnPdOx held 0.45 V overpotential at 10 mA/cm², within 40 mV of their RuOx (0.41 V); PdOx passed 0.5 V at about 200 h and NiTaPdOx at about 470 h. It calls the platform human-supervised with over 90% automation; operators move sample fixtures and start instruments.

title: LLM recipe generator guides the first synthesis of three unreported oxy-selenides; humans ran the furnace
who: Jeon, Kim, … Li, Cho (Sungkyunkwan University, Ajou University, KICET, MIT) · Advanced Materials 38, e74502
what: A retrieval-augmented language model built on recipes extracted from 4,407 papers proposed solid-state routes for DFT-screened solid-electrolyte candidates. Fed back XRD results, it brought LiCr(SeO₃)₂ to single phase at 400 °C, then LiAl(SeO₃)₂ and CsLiSeO₄ in three guided experiments each, and found a new route to the known LiGa(SeO₃)₂.
caveat: Humans chose the targets by first-principles screening and did every synthesis step (mortar, tube furnace, XRD) themselves; the model's claimed contribution is fewer trial-and-error cycles. Three new compounds from one group, published 10 Aug 2026, no independent replication yet

title: Reinforcement learning controls the plasma in a tokamak
who: Google DeepMind + EPFL Swiss Plasma Center · Nature
what: A single RL controller shaped and held plasma configurations in the TCV tokamak, including shapes not previously produced there.
artifact: Live control of a fusion experiment
caveat: A control-engineering result, not new plasma physics

title: GraphCast beats ECMWF's operational forecast on 90% of targets; GenCast beats the ensemble on 97%
who: Google DeepMind · Science (2023), Nature (2024)
what: Learned weather models outperform the leading physics-based system at 10-day forecasts; ECMWF now runs its own learned model operationally.
artifact: Operational forecasts used by weather services
caveat: Prediction, not explanation; trained on physics-model reanalysis

title: Physics-tailored neural network reveals unexpected non-reciprocal forces in dusty plasma, confirmed by experiment
who: Emory University (Burton, Nemenman) · PNAS 122(31)
what: A custom physics-structured network trained on 3D particle tracks described non-reciprocal interparticle forces with >99% accuracy and showed two textbook assumptions (charge–size relation, screening-length dependence) are wrong; follow-up experiments confirmed it.
caveat: Small system; custom architecture, not a general model

title: Unstable self-similar singularities found in fluid equations with physics-informed neural networks
who: Google DeepMind, Brown, NYU, Stanford · arXiv 2509.14185
what: New families of unstable blow-up profiles for incompressible porous media and 3D Euler with boundary, to near machine precision.
caveat: Framed as groundwork for Navier–Stokes; experts note real fluids have no singularity

title: GPT-5 science paper: black-hole symmetries, cosmic-string gravitational-wave spectra, thermonuclear burn modeling
who: OpenAI with Lupsasca, Scherrer, Spears (LLNL) · arXiv 2511.16072
what: Case studies where GPT-5 contributed derivations or reduced-physics models; the burn-propagation case produced a working ridge-map code for inertial-confinement fusion modeling.
caveat: Company-curated case studies; mixed novelty

title: GPT-5.2 Pro proposes a new gluon scattering-amplitude formula; OpenAI model proves it
who: Guevara (IAS), Lupsasca, Skinner, Strominger, Weil · arXiv 2602.12176
what: For one negative-helicity gluon the tree amplitude, assumed zero, is nonzero on a special slice of momentum space; the model proposed the closed form after humans computed cases to n = 6. Arkani-Hamed and Craig commented favorably.
caveat: Preprint; no experimental consequence claimed

title: Claude computes the nine-loop six-point amplitude in planar N=4 super Yang–Mills
who: Anthropic (Fitzpatrick, Mishra-Sharma), checked by Dixon; von Hippel's public challenge
what: Previous record was eight loops (2023). Two internal representations agreed on all 107,053 nonzero coefficients at symbol level (the beyond-symbol completion was computed once, with no second independent computation); the bootstrap took about $100 of CPU (96 CPUs for a week), and von Hippel puts either approach at one to two thousand dollars once Claude's time is counted.
caveat: A record computation in a toy model, by known methods; von Hippel says it did not produce the new methods he hoped for

title: Navier–Stokes finite-time singularity under smooth forcing (Clay statements C and D), Lean-formalized
who: OpenAI internal model, ~10,000 agents · Sept 8 2026
what: Blow-up from a smooth fluid at rest under a smooth external force. Clay called the problem 'apparently settled' (Sept 11) with review ongoing; OpenAI is not claiming the prize.
caveat: Unforced case still open. Bastounis–Circelli–Hansen (arXiv 2610.08144) show the Lean code and the 166-page paper are not the same proof (a Lean lemma needs m+5 derivatives where the paper claims m+4) while explicitly not claiming either is wrong. Says where the continuum model breaks, nothing about real fluids. Hales (guest post on Tao's blog, 9 Oct 2026) reports the Lean formalisation 'has already been confirmed by more than a dozen proof-checkers'; the open question is whether the Lean statement is the paper's theorem, not whether the Lean proof checks.

title: OpenAI's 372-family release: 70 families in PDE, mathematical physics, quantum information and statistical physics
who: OpenAI unreleased internal model · github.com/openai/math, Oct 6 2026
what: Includes universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes, De Giorgi in dimension 8, a uniform Hilbert's 16th bound, Parity ∉ QAC⁰. About 42% (300 of 719) of top-line results Lean-formalised; 3 manuscripts withdrawn Oct 7 (722 to 719).
caveat: Mostly unreviewed; no human has yet read most of them. The 70 is the catalogue's own sections Mathematical physics (25, which hold the quantum-information families), Partial differential equations (16) and Probability and statistical mechanics (29). 'No human has read most of them' is the author's inference: the repository says the manuscripts came from a fixed model-driven procedure, that some unformalised results 'could have issues', and that one writeup was human-edited; it does not say who has read them.
